page.layout: One printed page: running head at top with page number left; a large engraving (woodcut illustration) in the centre; below it a four-line verse epigram in italic; a small signature mark "De" at the lower right.

p.i: Laudatur virtus, sed non transfertur ad vsum,
Dic mihi, quid, quaeso? vanius esse potest?
Horrida diuinae quis non incendia sentit
Irae? quis vero nunc respicit? ai,

page.notes: The engraving shows a tower with barred windows, a half-naked captive woman and children at a chest, a merchant weighing coins, and two men in hats and a cloak at right, with a distant castle on a hill. The verse lines are set as printed; the last line ends in an unclear word, and "ai" is the printed end of the epigram. The "De" at lower right is a signature-like mark, not a gathering signature. The running head is set in small capitals and reads EMBLEMA; the title CAPTIVA VIRTVS is set in italic capitals under it.
